page: Microsoft Azure M176-88bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz, configured with 44 physical cores and 88 vCPUs via hyperthreading on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system features 1536.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 17.45 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a 410 GB local disk, and the instance is premium storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, with large-block read-only and write operations placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by top-tier Geekbench multi-core and software compilation scores. Database operations also rank in the top 10% according to Passmark benchmarks. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and bzip3 decompression single-threaded benchmarks scoring in the average range.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and top-tier memory bandwidth, this server is designed for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and complex data processing. The inclusion of Intel Advanced Vector Extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions supports strong performance in medium-model LLM inference prompt processing. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of 1.5 TB of RAM paired with 88 vCPUs minimizes the need for multi-node clustering for large datasets, though the lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training.
